text: The seven Glyphs SDK plugin base classes over a plugin host (R025). They follow GlyphsSDK ObjectWrapper/GlyphsApp/plugins.py : the same defaults in init / loadPlugin , then the optional script hooks settings() and start() ; titles from menuName / name ; filters call filter(layer, inEditView, customParameters) ; reporters call foreground / background / inactiveLayerForeground / inactiveLayerBackground with getScale() set from the paint context. Exceptions in protocol methods go to the environment's error sink, as the SDK sends them to LogError . make_plugins_module(env) returns the GlyphsApp.plugins module with classes bound to env .

text: The plugin host contract on FontLab 9 (R025-R027). What this module keeps (Glyphs-specific): Menus: Glyphs menu names map to FontLab's main-window menus by title (FILE "File", EDIT "Edit", VIEW "View", GLYPH "Glyph", PATH "Contour", WINDOW "Window", SCRIPT "Script", HELP "Help"); FILTER_MENU and APP_MENU have no FontLab counterpart and go to an owned "Glyphs Plugins" menu. Each NSMenuItem becomes an owned QAction; its triggered runs item.fire() through the error sink, and item changes (title, state, enabled) update it. Panels and filter dialogs are owned tool windows (FontLab's own panel registry is not scriptable here); a dialog closes with Apply or Cancel. Painters go to the session's editor painters: native canvas painters ( drawing.native_painters ) when the build has them, else the overlay :class: ~fontlab_glyport.drawing.editor.EditorPainters . Tools: flWorkspace.registerPythonTool with a :class: ~fontlab_glyport.plugins.tool_bridge.ToolBridge ; builds without it raise UnsupportedCapability . Tools have no icon yet (SDK icons are PDF resources). File formats: a File-menu action "Export with <title>…" calls exportFont_ with the current font. Layers, fonts, snapshots and undo come from an injected model adapter (the GlyphsApp model of lane L1); without one those calls raise. What App provides (generic): FontLabPluginHost is a :class: fontlabapp.qt.menus.OwnedMenus . That class adds the QActions, shows the tool windows, hands out the tokens and tears everything down. Its rules hold here unchanged: every token removes its widgets and connections exactly once; close() removes everything newest first, tries each item and re-raises the first failure. Nothing is disconnected or deleted while a signal of the host's own widgets dispatches (the PythonQtSignalReceiver crash pattern in AGENTS.md). Teardown, and any remove / close called from a host slot (menu action, Apply/Cancel, title-bar close, on_close callback), wait for App's shared zero-delay timer. Why a subclass: OwnedMenus already has the seams this host needs ( _token , _menu , _defer(first=True) , _guarded ), so the subclass adds only Glyphs mapping, NSMenuItem sync and the Apply/Cancel dialog. It never edits App's private queue. A missing main window is App's qtsafe.MainWindowNotFound ; the host reports it as HostUnavailable .

text: Load a plugin class into a host and unload it deterministically (R025-R027). load_plugin(cls, env) creates the instance the SDK way ( alloc().init() then loadPlugin() ) and registers what its protocol needs: FilterWithoutDialog: a FILTER_MENU item running filter(layer, True, {}) on the selected layers inside one undo group. FilterWithDialog: a FILTER_MENU item that snapshots the selected layers, opens the plugin's view in a host dialog ( setup() previews), keeps the result on Apply and restores the snapshots on Cancel, in one undo group. PalettePlugin: a host panel with theView() . ReporterPlugin: a VIEW_MENU toggle "Show <title>"; while on, painters for each hook the plugin defines (foreground/background, active/inactive). If the host refuses before-native drawing (FontLab R054), background hooks paint in the post-native overlay. REPORTER_BACKGROUND_AS_OVERLAY records "background drawn as overlay" in the execution receipt: ink is above the native outlines, rather than below them. SelectTool: register_tool ; its foreground/background paint while it is active. FileFormatPlugin: register_file_format . GeneralPlugin: nothing; its start() adds menus through Glyphs.menu . A register_* call the host cannot honour ( UnsupportedCapability ) becomes a diagnostic; the rest of the plugin stays loaded. A failure in init / loadPlugin gives a failed handle with everything registered so far removed (R027). unload() removes tokens newest first, once.

text: A Glyphs SelectTool as a FontLab Python tool ( registerPythonTool ). FontLab calls the bridge with Qt events of a glyph canvas viewport: mousePressed/Moved/Released/DoubleClicked(event, canvas) , keyPressed/Released(event, canvas) and activate / deactivate . The bridge makes the Glyphs call: mouseDown_ , mouseDragged_ (a move with a button down) or mouseMoved_ , mouseUp_ , mouseDoubleDown_ (else mouseDown_ with clickCount() == 2 ), keyDown_ and keyUp_ . The NSEvent is copied eagerly: FontLab invalidates the Qt event after the call. While a call runs, Glyphs.currentEvent() is that event, and tool.editViewController().graphicView() maps it to glyph units of the active glyph ( getActiveLocation_ ) through App's paint-context maths. A mouse event is handled (FontLab's own tool skips it) only when the plugin overrides the method. Keys are delivered but never claimed: FontLab also sends ShortcutOverride as keyPressed , and claiming it would swallow every menu shortcut while the tool is active. activate / deactivate run the loader's callbacks (which add and remove the tool's foreground/background painters) and the SDK's willActivate / willDeactivate . Every plugin call goes through guard , and no exception from any callback reaches FontLab: it goes to sink .

text: Container views a NIB can hold (R031): NSStackView , NSScrollView , NSBox , NSSplitView , NSGridView , NSVisualEffectView . A stack view is a frame-based container, like every NIB view here (Auto Layout constraints are not solved). Views loaded from a NIB keep Interface Builder's frames. When the arranged views change (added, inserted, removed, hidden with detachesHiddenViews ) or the orientation, spacing, alignment or insets are set, the stack places its arranged views again: along the axis from the leading edge (top-down when vertical, Cocoa's y decreasing), spacing apart, inside edgeInsets , each at its current size, and aligned on the other axis (leading/top, trailing/bottom, else centred). Distributions: gravity areas and fill keep sizes (fill's stretched view depends on hugging priorities, which are not decoded); fill equally/proportionally resize along the axis; equal spacing/centering spread the views. The stack view does not resize itself.

text: Read compiled NIBs (no Objective-C runtime) into plain Python objects (R031). Two container formats occur in Glyphs plugin bundles: NIBArchive (the default since macOS 10.13; a single file or keyedobjects-101300.nib ) and NSKeyedArchiver binary plists ( keyedobjects.nib ). Both decode to the same shape: :class: Archived objects (class name plus fields) with strings, numbers and collections already turned into Python values. A .nib directory is read through its keyed archive when present. NIBArchive layout, all integers little-endian: magic, two format words, then (count, offset) pairs for objects, keys, values and class names. Variable integers keep 7 bits per byte, and a set high bit marks the last byte. Value types: 0-3 signed ints of 1/2/4/8 bytes, 4 false, 5 true, 6 float, 7 double, 8 data (length-prefixed), 9 nil, 10 object reference (4 bytes). Collections store their elements under the repeated key UINibEncoderEmptyKey . Hostile input is rejected with :class: NibFormatError , never expanded: files over MAX_BYTES , variable integers wider than 5 bytes (32 bits), table counts larger than the file, offsets and references outside their tables, reference chains deeper than MAX_DECODE_DEPTH , and any malformed record. Shared and cyclic references decode once (memoised by object index).

text: XIB sources and compiled NIBs as one UIGraph (R028, R031). Both readers emit the same node schema, so a NIB with no XIB source and the XIB it came from produce equal graphs (the tests compare them): source_class is the AppKit class ( NSTextField ); a custom class is in properties["customClass"] ( GSSteppingTextField , GSPaletteView ). Placeholders are NSCustomObject nodes with properties["role"] : owner (File's Owner, with className ), firstResponder or application ; other custom objects have role object . Views carry frame [x, y, w, h] in Cocoa's bottom-left coordinates, autoresizingMask (Interface Builder's default 12, top-left pinned) and hidden . Controls add the keys their class uses: title , editable , bezeled , buttonType , state , minValue , maxValue , value , items , selectedIndex , continuous , enabled , toolTip . Connections: outlet (owner node -> destination, selector = property; an outlet to a control's cell points at the control), action (control -> target, selector = action), binding (control -> controller, selector = binding name, argument = key path), constraint (first item -> second item, or the first item again for a constant; selector "<attribute> <relation> <attribute>" , argument "<multiplier> <constant> <priority>" ). A tab view's items are its child NSView pages with tabLabel and tabIdentifier ; text fields with a number formatter carry formatter {"minimum", "maximum"} , and a standalone formatter is an NSNumberFormatter node with the limits it sets; progress indicators carry minValue , maxValue , value and indeterminate . A matrix carries rows , columns , mode , cellSize , intercellSpacing and cells : row-major button cells, each with title , buttonType , state , tag and enabled . A box carries boxType , titlePosition , borderType , transparent and title ( "" when no title is shown); its only child is its content view, marked contentView . A scroll view carries hasVerticalScroller , hasHorizontalScroller , autohidesScrollers and a custom clipViewClass ; its only child is its clip view's document view, marked documentView (the clip view and scrollers are not nodes). An array controller is an NSArrayController node; each table column is also an NSTableColumn child node ( index ) so bindings can name it. A table view carries columns ( identifier , title , width , minWidth , maxWidth , editable ), headerVisible , allowsMultipleSelection , rowHeight and prototypes : for a view-based table, each prototype cell view as its own graph JSON keyed by identifier (File's Owner = the makeViewWithIdentifier_owner_ owner). Buttons also carry bordered and, with a named image, image and imagePosition ; a switch carries state . A text view carries string (plain text), editable and selectable . A split view carries vertical and dividerStyle (its subviews are the panes); a grid view carries rows , columns , rowSpacing and columnSpacing (its cells' content views are its children); a visual effect view is a plain container. A segmented control carries segments ( label , width , selected , tag , image ) and trackingMode ; a search field adds placeholder and sendsSearchStringImmediately to the text field properties. A combo box carries title (its text), editable , items , completes , numberOfVisibleItems and usesDataSource . A path control carries url (a URL string), editable and allowedTypes . An image view carries image (a resource name) and imageScaling . A stack view carries orientation (0 horizontal, 1 vertical), alignment (an NSLayoutAttribute), distribution , spacing , edgeInsets [top, left, bottom, right] and detachesHiddenViews ; its children (the arranged views) carry arranged . A window ( NSWindow or NSPanel ; a custom subclass in customClass ) carries title , styleMask and contentRect (screen coordinates, bottom-left); its content view is its only child, marked contentView . Nodes keep document order (XIB) or archive order of NSSubviews (NIB). Elements the readers do not translate still become nodes (class xib:<element> or the archived class); the loader decides what is blocked.
